newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rebels say ready for talks but set ultimatum.
newsitem.headline: Rebels say ready for talks but set ultimatum.

text.p: Officials of the Zaire rebel army of Laurent Kabila said on Friday they were in South Africa and ready to talk peace but Zaire government envoys did not appear to be serious about negotiating.
"We give them until tomorrow to decide. We came for the talks and we are ready," Bizima Karaha, Kabila's foreign affairs commissioner, told Reuters in Johannesburg.
Karaha, speaking from Pretoria, said that city had been designated as the venue for the negotiations, but added:
"The Zaireans are not very serious. We are very disappointed. We arrived last night for the talks but have had no response from the Zaireans. Their people are lazy."
South Africa, which is facilitating the meeting, had expected to announce the schedule and venue of the peace talks by Friday afternoon, but has made no official statements.
A senior South African diplomat in London, however, hinted at a likely delay saying "there won't be any discussions if the two parties are not there".
